chapter: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
title: The 1953 three-band package show with Little Richard
summary: He booked and led a theater package with Little Richard's band, his own six-piece and a six-piece girl band, and trouble started when a promoter ran off with deposits.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: -- the International Sweethearts to hearts of rhythm. Then we had the Cavalcade of Jazz with Jack Teagarden. Now, that takes you up, oh, then there's the period with Winonie Harris. Now, that takes up to '53. My information says you continued regular arranging, including for and playing with Swingers, Inc. I don't know. What do you remember from that period after you were finished with Winonie?
Yeah.

Well, I organized the show. I think (inaudible) nine years, went on down into Richmond, Norfolk, Newport, Georgia. Within that show, I had three bands traveling and Little Richard's band (inaudible) five-piece band and I had my band, which was six pieces, boys, and had a six-piece girl band.
When you say boys, were they youngsters or --
No, the guys that was with me, you know, C.C. Williams, Freddie Benito, (inaudible).
(Inaudible).
On drums. He's in town here. He plays with some of the guys (inaudible). And well, I won't name them. I had five or six pieces with me. My brother was with me.
Which one?
The piano player. He was with me. This show included a dancer called Sonya Millburn. I don't know if you remember her or not.
(Inaudible).

And I had this Sandman with me that was on the tour with Basie with me and Tommy Tucker, blues singer, and I had Elaine, the girl had kind of a hit record, that was like -- what was her name? She was doing good with a record. Had a big show. I put this show together.
Yeah. Well, who booked it?
I booked it myself.
Oh, yeah? You had got the contacts, had you?
Yeah, had the contacts (inaudible).
Did you make any money?

Yeah, but I only -- got off to a bad start was when I got out in Georgia, the promoter, one of the promoters started running off with the deposits. Caught up with him and he got put in jail (inaudible), caused a lot of trouble. So we stayed out quite a few weeks. I had the three bands together. Yeah, we made money.
Well, now, was Little Richard hot already then?
No, he just got hot about two or three
months. He was recording then and he got real hot right after that.
: Yes.

Five or six pieces. I remember, I opened up on the stage, big stages in ______, Atlanta, and I would have Little Richard's band on this side, have my band on this side, and the girl band right in the middle. So, that included about 17, 18 pieces.
: Well, I mean, did you all play together?
We played the opening together (inaudible).
: Yeah. What would you play to open up?
I've forgotten.
: No, I mean, it would be something like an instrumental?

Yeah, opening, yeah, stage opening. I think Little Richard would do the blues and we'd open up all together with it. Feature some guys in my band and feature girls on the sides and then on to somebody else and in the end, Little Richard would come out and sing and we'd close the curtain. And when you close the curtain, you open it back up with the girls band, had moved into the center. No, they were in the center. Then they would do specialty.
